_comment: The in-wallet swap fee, per chain. Edited by ops, shipped in the build.
`recipient` is where the Universal Router's PAY_PORTION sends the wallet's
share. Null disables in-wallet swap on that chain — that is the whole gate.
Five named tiers. `baseName`/`baseBips` are tier 0, what everyone pays before
holding anything; `tiers` are the four rungs above it, in ascending order.
The ladder reads as a scale of generated power: Static, Charge, Magneto,
Turbine, Reactor. The names are disjoint from the API credit tiers
(Spark, Arc, Surge, Storm) and from the DYNO token's own name, Dynamo —
two ElectroSwap holder ladders sharing a word read as one programme.
services/api src/config/walletFeeTiers.ts is the authority; this file is
the offline fallback and the ceiling (see fees.ts).
`minScore` is a BOLT-equivalent score, 18 decimals, as a decimal string. The
thresholds were chosen to mean roughly $25 / $250 / $1,250 / $2,500 of BOLT
at the price when they were set (2026-09), and BOLT's price moves, so the USD
meaning drifts. Recompute them here when it has drifted far enough to matter —
that is a text edit and a release, not an owner transaction.
`dynoWeight` is BOLT-equivalent per DYNO, 18 decimals (875.68 BOLT per DYNO).
It is an anchor, not the last word: the wallet measures the real ratio as a
time-weighted average of the two prices over the past week and uses that
when it has one. This number is what it falls back to — on a build with no
indexer, on a week too thin to average, or when the last measurement has
gone stale — and it is what the measurement is clamped against.
`dynoWeightBand` is that clamp: a measurement may be at most this many times
the anchor, and at least the anchor divided by it. It exists so a broken or
manipulated feed cannot hand somebody the top tier or stop a real holder
reaching theirs; it is a backstop, not a tuning knob. 1 or less turns the
measurement off and pins the weight to `dynoWeight`.
`countFarmBolt` is false because counting staked BOLT needs a read the wallet
does not make: the on-chain schedule did it from its own farm-id list. Turning
it on means teaching HolderService to read the farm, not just flipping this.
Testnet has no recipient, so in-wallet swap is off there until a dev sets one
through `holder.configure` — which the config permits precisely because this
chain names none. Its ladder is a short one for exercising the tiers; tBOLT
does not exist, so only DYNO scores, at 1 BOLT-eq each — and with no BOLT
price to divide by there is nothing to measure, hence a band of 0.
